Units and techniques

You draft 3 of these 5 units. They grow during the run by learning techniques: every won fight (except the boss and the Moon Shrine) offers 3 that your units can learn; one unit learns one, or you skip for 8 gold. Shops sell them too (15 gold common, 24 rare). Each technique belongs to one line, and some need another first. A unit's level is the number of different techniques it has learned; forgetting one (at a shop) keeps the level, and relearning it adds none.

Necromancer

HP 14 · DMG 4 · RNG 3 · AP 1 · MV 1 · Medium

Boss. Brings raised versions of the factions you beat this act, and raises your fallen against you. One action a turn: blows up a bone pile your units stand on or next to, raises every bone pile within 4 tiles at once, or fires a bolt. Keeps 2 tiles away, walks up to bolt range and shoots (needs line of sight).

  • Bolt (1 AP): 4 damage up to 3 tiles away, needs line of sight.
  • Corpse Blast (1 AP, cooldown 2): a bone pile within its raise range explodes for 2 damage in the 3x3 around it, friend or foe; the pile is used up.
  • Raise (1 AP, cooldown 3): brings every one of its side's bone piles within 4 tiles back at full HP at once, unless someone stands on it. The raised unit acts from the next enemy turn.
  • Soul Harvest: while it is on the board your units that die leave a bone pile; raising one brings it back on its side as a Bone version with only its basic attack.
  • Stone Heart: its HP falls in 3 phases, and it loses at most one a round: damage past the next phase is lost until your next turn. Each new phase changes how it fights (Giant: 2 actions a turn, then falling rocks on your units' tiles each round; Necromancer: 2 skeletons climb onto the roof). Its max HP grows by 1 for every level in your army.

AI: Necromancer

Each new phase changes how it fights (Giant: 2 actions a turn, then falling rocks on your units' tiles each round; Necromancer: 2 skeletons climb onto the roof). Its max HP grows by 1 for every level in your army.

Enemy AI

How enemies decide what to do. The rules every enemy shares come first; each behaviour below only lists what it does differently.

The enemy turn

  • At the start of the enemy phase, burning ground and poison tick, then every enemy gets its 1 AP back (unused AP doesn't carry over) and its moves (1, or 2 with Swift; none if pinned). A slowed enemy can move or act, not both: one that can hit from where it stands does, and it never backs off.
  • Next, every bomb on the board explodes, one by one (a blast sets off other bombs and mines inside it).
  • Then the enemies act one at a time, in the order they entered the battle. Each finishes its whole turn before the next starts. Units raised or split off during this phase wait until the next enemy turn.
  • A turn is a loop: the enemy picks a target, does the first thing on its behaviour's list that it can, and starts over. It stops when it runs out of AP and moves, or nothing on the list helps. The target is picked again before every action, so after a kill it turns to the next one.
  • Enemies move by your rules: 1 move per tile (moves are separate from AP), no diagonals, stepping out of a tile next to one of your units uses up their remaining moves (zone of control), no moving after spending AP, pinned units can't move, and slowed units can move or act but not both.
  • Enemies can't see mines, except a goblin standing next to one, which can fling it. One that steps on a mine stops there and sets it off.
  • Enemies walk through burning ground but never stop on it. One with nobody to hit attacks a barricade or rubble in its reach.

Targeting

  1. A unit that used Taunt within 2 tiles: the nearest such unit. It is then the only unit this enemy aims attacks or abilities at (area hits like the Giant's Smash and Slam still hit everyone in them).
  2. Blood Scent (wolves): the lowest-HP unit it can reach and attack this turn, walking up first if needed.
  3. Otherwise the nearest of your units, counted in steps and ignoring rocks. Ties go to the one with the lowest HP, then to the one listed first in your army. If that unit has a shield, it goes for the nearest unshielded unit it can reach this turn instead, and hits the shield only when there is none.

Every behaviour uses this target. Only the Bomber may bomb a different unit when its target can't be bombed, and the Necromancer raises bone piles before it looks for a target at all.

Walking up

  1. If it has its AP and can reach a tile from which it can hit the target, it walks to the cheapest such tile. Ranged units need range and line of sight from that tile.
  2. Otherwise it walks as close to the target as it can: to the reachable tile with the shortest walk to any tile next to the target, the cheapest of those. That walk goes around rocks but through units, so an enemy stuck behind its friends still edges forward.
  3. If no reachable tile is closer than where it stands, it stays put.

Ranged enemies that walk up (the Crossbowman) walk to the cheapest tile with a shot. They don't look for cover; the Camp layout just starts them behind rocks.

Backing off

Used by enemies that want distance, once per turn, when their target is too close: it moves to the reachable tile furthest from the nearest of your units, the cheapest of those. If no tile is further away than where it stands, it stays.

Getting into range from a distance

Used by enemies that fight from afar, once per turn. They only consider tiles at least their comfort distance from every one of your units:

  1. The cheapest tile from which it can use its ranged action on the target, if it still has the AP for it.
  2. If there is none, the tile closest to the target, if it is closer than where it stands.

Behaviours

BehaviourEach loop, the first that appliesUsed by
Walk up and hit
  1. If it can hit its target from where it stands: attack, or Bull Rush instead when it has it ready (Bandit Brute), or Grasp instead when it has it ready and the target is ranged or Swift and not already pinned (Skeleton), or Rending Blow instead when it has it ready and more than 2 HP (Demon).
  2. Fire Breath when it has it ready (Fiend): from its tile or one it can walk to, at whichever of your units puts the most of them in the line; it beats a strike.
  3. Otherwise walk up to it.
Wolf, Bandit Brute, Shard, Demon, Fiend, Skeleton, Totem, Bone Wolf, Bone Shard
Thief
  1. Carrying stolen gold: if it is on the enemies' back row, escape with the gold. Otherwise move to the reachable tile furthest back (the cheapest of those). Once it can't get any further back this turn: if it ran, it drops caltrops on the free tile next to it nearest your units; if it's cornered, it strikes whoever it can. Light Fingers lets it run in the same turn it steals.
  2. Not carrying gold: attack its target if it can, otherwise walk up, like Walk up and hit. Its first hit that does damage steals the gold, and it spends the rest of its moves running.
Cutpurse
Bomber
  1. If its target is closer than 2 tiles: back off (once a turn).
  2. Bomb its target if it can; if not, the nearest of your units it can bomb (once a turn).
  3. If the target is next to it: stab.
  4. If it hasn't bombed yet: get into range for a bomb (once a turn), with a comfort distance of 2.
Goblin Bomber, Bone Goblin Bomber
Giant
  1. With its action (two actions a turn from its second phase, Wrath; it loops until both are spent): smash or slam, whichever deals more in total (slam needs 2 or more of your units within 2 tiles; 3 damage to each), ties going to smash.
  2. Or, with nobody close enough for either: throw a boulder at its target if it is 2 to throw-range tiles away and the rock wouldn't block the Giant's own way to it.
  3. Without an action to take: walk up to the target, then try again.
Giant
Shooter
  1. If it can shoot its target from where it stands: shoot.
  2. Otherwise walk to the cheapest tile with a shot, preferring one next to a wall (Behind Cover), and shoot.
  3. With no shot this turn: walk closer, into cover if it can, then go on Overwatch if it's ready.
Crossbowman, Bone Crossbowman
Goblin
  1. If a bomb or mine lies on an empty tile next to it: fling it at its target, or at the nearest of your units 2-4 tiles away.
  2. If it can hit its target from where it stands: strike.
  3. If it can't reach anyone to strike this turn: fling a goblin next to it that hasn't acted at its target, or at the nearest of your units 2-4 tiles away.
  4. Otherwise walk up to it (Elusive: your reach doesn't stop it), then try again.
Goblin
Pack Leader
  1. It acts before every other enemy.
  2. Howl (its action for the turn) if the extra move lets at least one wolf that hasn't acted reach and bite its target this turn, or at least two if the leader could bite someone itself.
  3. Then like Walk up and hit: bite if it still has its AP, otherwise walk up.
Pack Leader
Elemental
  1. If it can hit its target from where it stands: strike.
  2. If it can reach a tile to strike from this turn: walk up and strike.
  3. Otherwise walk as close as it can, then use Upheaval on its target, or on the nearest of your units within 2 tiles.
Elemental
Necromancer
  1. If its target is closer than 2 tiles: back off (once a turn).
  2. If blowing up a bone pile in range (its side's or one of your fallen) would hit more of your units than of its own, at least one: Corpse Blast, the pile with the most of yours first.
  3. Otherwise, if any bone pile it can raise is in range and free: raise them all, your fallen included (Soul Harvest).
  4. If it can hit the target from where it stands: fire a bolt.
  5. Otherwise get into range for a bolt (once a turn), with a comfort distance of 2. It never walks closer than that to shoot.
Necromancer
Imp
  1. Imps act before the other enemies (after any howl), so the unit they swap in meets demons that still have their turn.
  2. If Hellswap is ready: from its tile or one it can walk to that is next to a fighting ally, swap with one of your units 2-3 tiles away that isn't already in an enemy's reach, so your unit lands next to that ally. Ranged units first, then the tile next to the most allies, then the weakest unit, then the shortest walk.
  3. Otherwise like Walk up and hit.
Imp, Bone Imp
Devil
  1. If its target is closer than 2 tiles: back off (once a turn).
  2. If Soul Contract is ready and one of your units is within 3 tiles: sign it on the unit it would kill first, else the hardest hitter, else the weakest.
  3. If it can hit the target from where it stands: strike with the trident (Long Reach).
  4. Otherwise get into range for a strike, or for a contract when one is ready (once a turn), with a comfort distance of 2.
Devil

Hover intent

Hovering an enemy shows the first thing it would do if its turn started now. It is a forecast, not a promise: your moves change it, and it only shows the first action. Hold Alt to see every enemy's intent at once.

ShowsWhen (checked in this order)On the board
FleeIt carries stolen gold.The enemies' back row, where it will escape.
HowlIt can howl, and the extra move would let at least one wolf bite this turn that otherwise couldn't (two if the leader could bite itself).Every wolf.
HellswapAn imp with Hellswap ready and a swap that drops one of your units next to a fighting ally (see the Imp routine).The target, and the tile it will land on.
Soul ContractA devil with Soul Contract ready that would sign one in its coming turn, after backing off or walking up (its turn is played out on a copy of the board).The target, with an arrow.
Fire BreathA fiend with Fire Breath ready that can breathe at one of your units this turn, from its tile or one it can walk to.The target, and the tile it breathes from.
Rending BlowIt has Rending Blow ready, more than 2 HP, and can reach its target to attack this turn.The target, with an arrow.
FlingA goblin that can't reach anyone to strike this turn, with a bomb, mine or unacted goblin next to it and one of your units 2-3 tiles away.The target, the goblin to be thrown and its landing tile.
GraspIt grasps, Grasp is ready, it can reach its target to attack this turn, and the target is ranged or Swift and not already pinned.The target, with an arrow.
UpheavalIt has Upheaval ready, can't reach its target to strike this turn, and the target is within 2 tiles plus its moves. It may still pick a nearer unit once it has walked.The target, with an arrow.
SlamIt can slam, 2 or more of your units are within 2 tiles, and the slam would deal more in total than a smash.The area within 2 tiles.
Corpse BlastIt has Corpse Blast ready and a bone pile in range whose 3x3 holds more of your units than of its own (at least one).The 3x3 around the pile.
RaiseIt can raise and a bone pile it can raise (its own side's, or one of your fallen with Soul Harvest) is in raise range and free. AP isn't checked.The bone pile.
BombIt bombs and its target is 2 to bomb-range tiles away with no bomb on its tile. Otherwise it shows Attack, though it may still bomb another unit or back off.The target's tile, where the bomb lands.
SmashIt smashes and the target is next to it, or the target is out of boulder range.The ring around it and the target.
ThrowIt throws boulders and the target is 2 to throw-range tiles away.The target and the tile where the rock will land.
AttackAnything else, whether or not it can reach the target this turn.The target, with an arrow.

Encounters

Battles are on a 6x6 board; you place your army in the back two rows. Kill every enemy to win. Battles bring factions you haven't beaten yet, then normal-strength rematches; Act 1 ends with one of the bosses. Every encounter has a layout template: fixed rules, with the exact rocks and start tiles varied each time.

Factions

Wolf Pack Open Field

Open ground with a mirrored pair of rocks; the wolves start bunched around their leader.

Pack Leader, Wolf x3

Necromancer raises: Bone Wolf

Goblin Bombers Ridge

A broken ridge across the middle: three rocks with a gap between each; bombers lob over it from the back row.

Goblin Bomber x2, Goblin x3

Necromancer raises: Bone Goblin Bomber

Bandit Camp Camp

Two rocks of cover in the middle with a crossbowman behind each; cutpurses start on the flanks.

Crossbowman x2, Cutpurse x2, Bandit Brute

Necromancer raises: Bone Crossbowman

A mirrored pair of crystals; three elementals spread across the back.

Elemental x3

Necromancer raises: Bone Shard

Demons Hellmouth

A mirrored pair of rocks; the Demon holds the enemies' front row with an imp on each side, the Devil behind it and the Fiend on a flank.

Demon, Imp x2, Devil, Fiend

Necromancer raises: Bone Imp

A harder rematch of a faction you've beaten: more of the same enemies. High risk, high reward: normal gold, and its technique pick always holds a rare one.

Open ground with a mirrored pair of rocks; two packs, each bunched around its own leader.

Pack Leader x2, Wolf x4

A broken ridge across the middle (three rocks with gaps); four bombers lob over it from the back row.

Goblin Bomber x4, Goblin x4

Elite Bandit Camp Camp

Three separate rocks of cover in the middle with a crossbowman behind each, cutpurses on the flanks, two brutes in the centre.

Crossbowman x3, Cutpurse x2, Bandit Brute x2

A mirrored pair of crystals; four elementals spread across the back.

Elemental x4

A mirrored pair of rocks; two Demons on the front row with the imps between or beside them, the Devil behind, the Fiend in a back corner.

Demon x2, Imp x2, Devil, Fiend

Bosses

Necromancer Graveyard

Two tombstones in the middle. His army is raised from the factions you beat this act.

Necromancer, 1 raised unit from each faction you beat this act (Skeletons fill up to 4)

Giant Quarry

Open quarry with a pair of boulders; the Giant reshapes it with slams and thrown rocks.

Giant

Scenarios

Moon Shrine Moon Shrine

Defend the shrine in the middle for 5 enemy turns. Elementals come from every edge, and more arrive on turns 2 and 4.

Elemental x3, 1 more Elementals after enemy turns 1 and 3

Break the Ritual Totem Grounds

Three goblin totems stand on the far half. Smash them all before the summoning completes at the start of enemy turn 6.

Goblin Bomber x3, Goblin x2, 3 Totems

The Moon Shrine (15 HP) stands at the centre; you deploy within 2 steps of it. Survive 5 enemy turns and the ritual completes: you win and pick a blessing. If the shrine breaks, the fight is lost (no gold) and you take a random curse, but the run goes on. Losing the whole army still ends the run. Enemies go for the shrine unless one of your units is next to them (Taunt still wins). The shrine counts as your ally for Guard; your own blasts and volleys hurt it. Reinforcements arrive on edge tiles at least 3 steps from it.

Break the Ritual: 3 totems (6 HP) stand on the far half, guarded by goblins. Smash them all before the summoning completes at the start of enemy turn 6: you win, the guards flee, and you get the usual technique pick. If the summoning completes, the fight is lost (no gold) and you take a random curse; the run goes on. Guards go for whichever of your units is within 2 tiles of a totem; their own bombs don't hurt the totems. The shrine and totems can't attack, so they have no zone of control.

Run & map

  • Pick 1 of 3 random banners, then draft 3 different base units (2 with Third Wheel). Army size up to 4.
  • Act 1 has 12 steps; each step offers 2 nodes. At steps 1, 4, 6, 8, 10 both choices are fights, so every run has at least 5 fights before the boss. Step 9 offers one more optional battle; the last step is a boss (Necromancer or Giant).
  • A Battle brings a faction you haven't beaten yet; once you've met them all it's a normal-strength rematch. Step 1 only brings the easier factions (Wolf Pack, Goblin Bombers, Bandit Camp). An Elite (steps 6 and 10) is a harder rematch of a faction you've beaten. Both show their faction when you reach their step.
  • The two scenario fights sit at steps 4 and 8, next to a battle: the Moon Shrine at one, Break the Ritual at the other. Shops and ? events fill the rest.
  • Won battle: 10 gold + 5 per surviving unit (+5 for an ambush). Gold carried off by escaped cutpurses is lost.
  • Technique pick: every won fight except the boss and the Moon Shrine offers 3 techniques your units can learn; one unit learns one and goes up a level (not when relearning a forgotten one), or skip for 8 gold.
  • Shop: 3 techniques (15 gold common, 24 rare), 3 items, forgetting a technique for 8 gold, a random base-unit recruit for 15 gold (if the army has room), and one banner you don't hold yet for 20 gold. Also: mend a crack for 10 gold, and hone an action (cooldown 1 turn shorter for that unit, for the run; actions with cooldown 2 or more, once each) for 12 gold.
  • Every battle starts at full HP and dead units come back. Techniques, levels, items and shrine HP last the whole run.
  • Cracks: an army unit that falls in a fight you win (or a lost scenario) is cracked: -1 max HP until mended at a shop. The 3rd crack shatters it, and it leaves the army for good. Scars (from the Cracked Altar) are cracks that can't be mended.
  • Champions: from step 6, every battle and elite has a champion, its affix named on the node: the toughest enemy gets +3 max HP and one rule below. Winning pays +5 gold.
  • Bosses have Stone Heart (see Abilities) and +1 max HP for every level in your army. They never fall off the board or into a hole.

? events

EventWhat happens

Abandoned CartA random technique one of your units can learn (a new one gives a level) or a random item, or leave it.
GamblerPay 10 gold for a 50% chance at 25.

SculptorFrom step 5: one unit gives up a technique you choose for a random rare one of its line (no level).
Hooded Stranger30 gold for a random curse.

Blessings and curses

Hold the Moon Shrine and pick a blessing. Lose a scenario fight and take a random curse (losing both gives two different curses). Either lasts the rest of the run and works every turn of every battle. Omens never pick the shrine itself.

SunAt the start of your turn, a sun sigil appears under an enemy. At the start of the enemy turn a sun beam strikes it for 3 damage, hitting whoever stands there.At the start of your turn, a sun sigil appears under one of your units. At the start of the enemy turn a sun beam strikes it for 3 damage, hitting whoever stands there.
NightAt the start of your turn, your unit and the 4 tiles next to it are shrouded until your next turn: enemies can't hit units there from range.At the start of your turn, an enemy unit and the 4 tiles next to it are shrouded until your next turn: your units can't hit units there from range.
MoonAt the start of your turn, your unit gets a shield that absorbs 4 damage until your next turn.At the start of your turn, an enemy unit gets a shield that absorbs 4 damage until your next turn.

Banners

A banner bends a rule for the whole army for the rest of the run. You start with one (pick 1 of 3), shops sell one you don't hold for 20 gold, and an elite offers one instead of its technique. No limit on how many you hold; each is held once. Taking Third Wheel with more units than it allows: choose who stays, the rest leave.

BannerRule
VampiricEvery attack of yours that deals damage heals the attacker 1. But the sun hunts you: every fight has the Curse of the Sun (a sun beam targets one of your units each turn, 3 damage).
Third WheelYour units get +1 AP and +1 move. But the army holds 2 units at most.
LoserA unit of yours that dies in a fight gets +1 max HP and +1 damage for the rest of the run (stacks).
MercenariesBefore each fight, hire 1 of 2 random base units for 8 gold. It fights for that battle only and doesn't count as a survivor for gold.
Battering RamYour units' pushes go 1 tile further and deal 2 damage.

AffixRule
Armoredtakes 1 less damage from everything (at least 1)
Vengefulwhen it dies, 2 damage to each of your units next to it
Regeneratingheals 2 at the start of its turn
Mighty+1 damage
Fleet+1 move

Battlefields

Every battle, elite and boss (and an ambush) has one battlefield rule, named on its map node from the start of the run, so you can route towards or around it. The scenario fights have none. A step's fights never share a battlefield or repeat one from the step before. Every rule works the same for both sides.

BattlefieldRule
Edge of the WorldA unit pushed off the board falls from the tower and dies, on either side. Nothing saves it, and it leaves no bone pile. Huge units can't be pushed.
StormAt the start of each round, lightning gathers over the tile under one of your units and one enemy. At the end of the enemy turn it strikes those tiles for 3 damage, hitting whoever stands there.
Arcane OverflowEvery action's cooldown is 1 shorter (1 at least), for both sides.
Fortune's FavoredAt the start of each round, one of your units and one enemy are favored: their attacks and blasts deal 2x damage until the next round. A boss is never favored.
What's On His Mind?You can't see what the enemies plan to do.
Crumbling RoofThe old roof gives way. A unit slammed into something, or a unit dying, fractures the tile it stands on; a tile fractured 2 times falls in. Whoever stands on it, or is pushed into a hole, falls and dies. Holes block walking but not shots. Huge units are too heavy to push in, and the Giant never falls.

Enemy AI: on Edge of the World an enemy that can push one of your units off the board with Bull Rush or Upheaval does that first. In a Storm, enemies never stop on a tile the lightning gathers over, and step off one before acting.

Battle rules

  • Moves are separate from AP: every unit walks 1 tile per turn (2 with Swift, +1 with Spring Boots), 4 directions, no diagonals. Units can walk through their allies (not through objectives) but can't stop on them, and never through enemies. Move first: once a unit spends AP (an attack or action) it can't move again that turn, for both sides. Unused moves don't carry over. AP pays for attacks and actions: every unit has 1 AP, so one attack or action per turn, and unused AP doesn't carry over. Blink, Vanish and Throw Shield (and Place Mine with Quick Fuse) are free, usable only before the unit has acted.
  • Cooldowns: basic attacks have none. Every other action, yours and the enemies', is ready again a set number of the unit's own turns after it's used (cooldown 2: used now, ready again two turns later).
  • Side phases: all your units act (one at a time), then all enemies.
  • Zone of control: stepping out of a tile next to an enemy uses up all your remaining moves, for both sides. You can always back off one tile, but you can't slip past.
  • Ranged attacks need line of sight (walls block it); Arcane Bolt ignores it. Bombs, boulders and fireballs are lobbed.
  • Mines: 4 damage (5 with Big Mines) to whoever stands on its tile, set off when an enemy steps on one (or a blast, fling or fireball sets it off). Bombs explode at the start of the next enemy turn and hit only their own tile. Fireballs and Volley hit a plus: the tile and its 4 neighbours. Blasts set each other off.
  • Push: a unit pushed into a wall, unit or the edge stops there and takes 2 damage. An enemy pushed onto a mine sets it off. Weight: a push moves a medium unit 1 tile, a small one 2 and a huge one none (no collision damage either); Battering Ram adds 1 tile to your pushes.
  • Poison: 2 damage at the start of the target's turn, 2 times. Burning ground: 1 damage at the start of the turn of whoever stands on it; enemies never stop on it.
  • Rubble (the Sapper's keyword): a low heap that blocks walking like a wall but not shots, and gives no cover. A unit pushed into it is crushed for 2 more than a normal collision (4 in all) and the rubble breaks. One hit from any unit clears it. Broken barricades collapse into rubble.
  • Pinned units (the Archer's keyword: Pinning Shot, Snare Trap, Suppressing Fire) can't move on their next turn. Slowed units (the Mage's keyword: Frost Nova, Chill, Blizzard) can move or act on their next turn, not both.
  • Hidden units (Vanish, Smoke Bomb, Into the Shadows) can't be targeted or attacked by enemies until your next turn, though area blasts still hit them. Attacking doesn't reveal them; the first attack while hidden deals +2.
  • Snares (Snare Trap) are hidden from enemies: the first enemy to walk onto one stops, takes damage and is pinned. The Archer's Overwatch is the Crossbowman's rule turned around: it shoots the first enemy that walks onto a tile the archer can shoot at, and stops it there.
  • Hover any enemy to see what it plans to do next.
  • Controls: left-click chooses (selects one of your units, or opens any unit's card; hover a name on the card for what it does), right-click acts (move, attack, or use the aimed action). Esc cancels an aimed action or closes the card.

Keywords

Rule texts use these words without explaining them; in the game, hovering one shows its meaning.

  • Pinned: Can't move on its next turn.
  • Slowed: On its next turn it can move or act, not both: walking costs it the attack, and acting ends its moves.
  • Marked: The next hit on it, by anyone and from anything but poison or fire, deals +2. Then the mark is gone.
  • Exposed: No ally of its own stands next to it.
  • Hidden: Until your next turn, enemies can't target or attack it (area blasts still hit). Attacking doesn't reveal it.
  • Burning: Burning ground: 1 damage to whoever starts a turn on it. Enemies walk through it but never stop on it.
  • Wall: A rock (crystals, tombstones and boulders too), ice or a barricade: blocks walking and shots, and gives cover. Rubble and holes are not walls.
  • Rubble: A low heap: blocks walking but not shots, and gives no cover. A unit pushed into it is crushed for 4 and the rubble breaks. One hit clears it.
  • Poison: 2 damage at the start of the target's turn, 2 times.
  • Push: A medium unit moves 1 tile, a small one 2, a huge one not at all. If it slams into a wall, a unit or the edge, it stops and takes 2. An enemy pushed onto a mine sets it off.
  • Zone of control: Stepping out of a tile next to an enemy uses up all remaining moves, for both sides.
  • Line of sight: Walls block shots. Bombs, boulders and fireballs are lobbed over them.
  • Fury: +1 damage per Fury for the rest of the fight, 3 at most.
  • Swift: 2 moves a turn instead of 1.
  • Shield: Absorbs damage before HP. Enemies go for an unshielded unit they can reach first, and hit a shield only when there is none.
  • Free: Costs no AP. Use it before the unit acts: it can still move and attack afterwards.
